title: COPENHAGEN
1167 TO NOW

cards.title: Bishop Absalon's castle
lines: A fortress on a tiny island guards a fishing village called Havn: "harbor".

cards.title: A real town
lines: Havn gets its town charter. Merchants start calling it "the merchants' harbor".

cards.title: København
lines: Køpmannæhafn, the merchants' harbor, slowly becomes the city's name.

cards.title: Castle destroyed
lines: The Hanseatic League tears down Absalon's castle. A new one soon rises.

cards.title: Capital of Denmark
lines: The king settles here for good. Copenhagen has ruled Denmark ever since.

cards.title: The Reformation
lines: Denmark turns Lutheran. Church lands pass to the crown.

cards.title: Rosenborg Castle
lines: Christian IV builds a summer house just outside the walls.

cards.title: Børsen
lines: A stock exchange crowned by four dragons with their tails twisted into a spire.

cards.title: The Round Tower
lines: An observatory with no stairs: a spiral ramp wide enough for a horse.

cards.title: The Swedish assault
lines: Swedish troops storm the walls at night. The city holds.

cards.title: Nyhavn
lines: A new canal brings ships right into the heart of the city.

cards.title: The plague
lines: About a third of the people in the city die in a single year.

cards.title: The Great Fire
lines: Three days of flames. 28% of the city burns and 15,000 people lose their homes.

cards.title: Christiansborg
lines: A new royal palace rises on Absalon's island.

cards.title: A golden spiral
lines: 400 steps up the spire of Our Saviour's Church, the last 150 outside.

cards.title: Frederiksstaden
lines: A new royal district: four palaces around one octagonal square.

cards.title: Left unfinished
lines: Too expensive: the Marble Church stands as a ruin for over 100 years.

cards.title: The palace burns
lines: Christiansborg burns down.

cards.title: The second fire
lines: 909 houses burn. 6,000 people lose their homes.

cards.title: British bombardment
lines: The Royal Navy shells the city for three nights. About 195 civilians are killed.

cards.title: Christiansborg II
lines: The palace is rebuilt in a sober classical style.

cards.title: Tivoli Gardens
lines: An amusement park opens just outside the city gate. It is still there.

cards.title: The walls come down
lines: For the first time in centuries, the city may build beyond its ramparts.

cards.title: The bridge quarters
lines: Nørrebro, Vesterbro, Østerbro. The population triples in 50 years.

cards.title: Work restarts
lines: After a century as a ruin, the Marble Church is finished.

cards.title: It burns again
lines: Christiansborg burns for the second time.

cards.title: The dome
lines: One of the largest church domes in Scandinavia.

cards.title: City Hall
lines: Its clock tower rises 105.6 meters over the new square.

cards.title: The Little Mermaid
lines: Too small to see from up here. This is where she sits.

cards.title: Christiansborg III
lines: The third palace gets the tallest tower in town: 106 meters.

cards.title: Grundtvig Church
lines: Yellow brick, built to look like a giant church organ.

cards.title: Occupation
lines: German troops occupy Denmark. The city is spared heavy bombing.

cards.title: The Shellhus raid
lines: An RAF raid on Gestapo headquarters also hits a school. 86 children are killed.

cards.title: SAS Royal Hotel
lines: Arne Jacobsen's hotel: Denmark's first skyscraper.

cards.title: Christiania
lines: Squatters take over an old military base and declare a free town.

cards.title: Back to the harbor
lines: Old docks turn into homes, offices and harbor baths.

cards.title: The Øresund Bridge
lines: 16 km of bridge and tunnel to Sweden. Malmö is now a commute away.

cards.title: The Opera House
lines: A gift to the nation from the Mærsk shipping family.

cards.title: The Royal Playhouse
lines: A theater built out over the water.

cards.title: CopenHill
lines: A power plant with a ski slope on its roof.

cards.title: Copenhagen
lines: About 670,000 people live in the city. Tivoli is still lit up every night.
